{"description":"pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:170-238

The doc comment says:

> `pkix-ct`'s `SignedCertificateTimestamp` does not carry an explicit
> `entry_type` field (it is implied by the delivery channel — cert
> extension ⇒ precert_entry, OCSP / TLS-handshake ⇒ x509_entry). This
> function unconditionally treats the SCT as `x509_entry`; the caller
> is responsible for picking the right entry point based on delivery
> channel.

This is a known design choice. The contract problem: when a caller
gets it wrong (passes a `precert_entry` SCT to `verify_sct_for_cert`,
or vice versa), the resulting failure is `Error::InvalidSignature`.

That diagnostic is indistinguishable from:

- Tampered SCT signature
- Wrong cert bytes (caller passed pre-cert when they should have
  passed final cert)
- Wrong log key (caller's log list was stale and the log key
  rotated)
- Right log key, wrong algorithm dispatch

…all of which are real failure modes. A caller debugging an
integration cannot tell from the error which one occurred.

This is a documentation contract failure: the doc warns the caller
to pick correctly, but provides no way to recover from picking
wrong. Three exits:

A. Add an `entry_type` field to `SignedCertificateTimestamp` derived
   from the delivery channel, and have the verifier dispatch
   automatically. The fields the caller would have set are now set
   by `from_extension_value` / `sct_list_from_tls_extension` /
   `sct_list_from_ocsp_response` — those constructors know which
   channel they parsed. This dissolves the issue entirely.

B. Return a typed `Error::EntryTypeMismatch` from the verifier when
   the signature would have verified under the OTHER entry type. The
   verifier would re-attempt with the alternate signed input on
   `InvalidSignature` and surface the alternative if it succeeds.
   Cost: 2x verification work on every error path.

C. Document the failure mode prominently and add a `try_both`
   convenience method on `SctVerifier`. Cheaper than B because the
   caller opts in.

Recommendation: A. The `entry_type` is wire-format information that
SHOULD be on the parsed type; it being implicit is a leak of the
parsing layer into the verification layer. PKIX-ppbr.19 is also a
defensive-code-forcing issue: every caller that handles SCTs from
mixed delivery channels (OCSP + TLS handshake + embedded) has to
maintain its own `(sct, channel)` association and route through the
right verifier.

Priority P1 because this is a contract decision that becomes harder
to make once the API ships and callers have written
delivery-channel-aware code on top.

Provenance: filed as PKIX-ppbr.19 on 2026-05-14, re-filed as PKIX-d4h.5 on 2026-06-15 with the description reduced to a pointer. PKIX-ppbr.19 is closed; this bead now carries its analysis verbatim."}

Fixed, but NOT by the beads recommended option A -- that option rests on a premise RFC 6962 does not support, and I checked the RFC rather than taking it.

Option A was: put an entry_type field on SignedCertificateTimestamp, set by whichever constructor parsed the SCT, and dispatch automatically; the bead called entry_type "wire-format information that SHOULD be on the parsed type".

It is not on the wire. RFC 6962 §3.2 (rfc6962.txt:676-692) puts LogEntryType INSIDE the digitally-signed structure, not in the transmitted SignedCertificateTimestamp. It is an INPUT to verification; no parser can recover it from an SCT.

Worse, the delivery channel settles it in only one direction. An embedded SCT is necessarily precert_entry -- the log signed it before the certificate now carrying it existed. But §3.3 names NO entry type for the TLS-handshake and OCSP channels: it requires only "the SCT data corresponding to the end-entity certificate", and a server may staple either kind. The existing doc claim "OCSP / TLS-handshake => x509_entry" is a deployment convention, not a protocol rule. Option A would have hardened that convention into the type system and made correct handling of a stapled precert SCT impossible -- a regression dressed as a fix.

What shipped instead supplies the information where it is actually available:

1. verify_sct_for_precert SELF-DIAGNOSES. It already holds the leaf DER that the x509_entry form signs over, so when its own check fails it asks the other question and returns the new Error::EntryTypeMismatch if that succeeds. Failure path only, so the bead-estimated "2x verification work" applies only when something already went wrong. The SCT is still REJECTED; this names a likely cause, it does not accept a signature.
2. verify_sct_for_cert CANNOT do that -- no issuer, so nothing to rebuild the PreCert structure from. That asymmetry is why the new SctVerifier::diagnose_entry_type exists: it takes both certificates and reports which entry type verifies, as the opt-in way out of an InvalidSignature that might be misrouting. This is closest to the beads option C, with Bs typed error for the case that can be detected for free.
3. LogEntryType is public and its rustdoc states that it is a verification input rather than a field of an SCT, and which channels do and do not determine it, so the next reader does not go hunting for it on the wire.
4. The doc note the bead called a contract failure ("the caller is responsible for picking the right entry point") now says what to do when they pick wrong, and no longer implies the channel determines the answer for OCSP and TLS.

Safety property pinned by test: a TAMPERED SCT verifies under no entry type and still reports InvalidSignature. The diagnosis must not launder a bad signature into a routing hint.

Fixture work: the x509-direction test needs an x509_entry SCT over a leaf that CARRIES an embedded SCT list, because verify_sct_for_precert strips that extension to rebuild the TBS and fails with LeafMissingSctList before any signature check when it is absent. sct-oracle/cert.der has no such extension, so it cannot be reused. Added gen_x509_entry_sct_over_precert_leaf.py, which signs an x509_entry SCT over precert-leaf-final.der with the precert oracles log key, reusing the existing generators builders so the oracle stays independent of pkix-ct. A final certificate logged as an x509 entry while also carrying embedded precert SCTs is an ordinary arrangement, not a contrivance.

Both new paths verified by mutation: removing the self-diagnosis returns InvalidSignature again; removing the diagnostics x509 arm makes it answer EntryTypeMismatch instead of Ok(X509).

Gates all green by exit code: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos (CI scope), 2379 tests, workspace feature powerset.
